relatedSnapshot.title: Banning a user does not cancel their subscription, so billing continues
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Banning or offboarding a user blocks app access but does not cancel their Autumn/Stripe subscription, so a locked-out customer keeps being billed until someone cancels billing manually.

## Problem

A customer whose account is banned cannot log in to cancel their subscription, and support cannot impersonate the banned account. The subscription keeps charging (e.g. $185/month Pro) until a billing admin cancels it separately.

## Root cause

Admin ban (apps/web/trpc/routers/admin/admin-users.ts banUser) sets only banned/banReason/banExpires and records an audit event; it never calls Autumn or Stripe. Cancellation is a separate flow (apps/web/trpc/routers/billing.ts cancelSubscription).

## Blast radius

488 banned users; 204 banned users across 237 organizations have billing history (billing_account.first_paid_observed_at not null). Exact count with currently-active subscriptions requires cross-referencing Autumn. Counted 2026-09-08.

## Proposed fix

Update the ban flow to offer "Cancel all and Ban" vs "Only Ban", actually cancelling active subscriptions with the provider before banning, and surfacing provider errors (do not ban when cancellation fails).

## What's included

Ban flow change to reconcile billing on ban. Prior art: ENG-10782 (same root cause, created 2026-06-24, outside the 30-day Slack intake window).

## Regression seam

banUser: banning a user with an active subscription must cancel it with the provider, or the admin must explicitly choose "Only Ban". Observable: a banned user has no active Autumn/Stripe subscription.

## Done when

* Banning a user with an active subscription cancels it with the provider (or prompts "Cancel all and Ban").
* Provider cancellation failure surfaces an error and does not ban the user.
* A regression test proves the ban flow cancels billing at the named seam.

## Reports

* ENG-13563

Order <uuid> (domain <domain>, created 2026-07-24 06:47Z) completed and is the bundle the customer actually uses (3 active connected inboxes). * 2026-08-23, 1800 cents ($18.00), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0021

relatedSnapshot.title: Name 7 — billed $1,436 for 18 inboxes never created, $144/month still renewing
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Bounded context: customer opened with "cancel all subscriptions and billing", then reported he has never had any inboxes or domains but is being charged for both; cancelling his legacy plan lowered the next bill by only $1; Manage Billing shows no subscription list to cancel; the remaining line item is labelled "inbox - inboxes - 18 x 8". He was escalated to a human and has had no answer.

Claim: 18 inboxes were charged at $8/month from 2025-12-03 to date, and $107.77 for 6 pre-warmed domains, but the workspace holds no domains or inboxes, has no outreach account connected, and the purchase record shows 0 of 18 mailbox creations succeeded, so the customer paid for a year of inbox capacity that never existed and has no self-serve control to stop the recurring charge.

Ask bucket: overcharged (money).

Verified money (Stripe, <stripe-id>): $1,554.08 USD collected across 12 paid invoices; nothing refunded; no credit notes; balance 0; no dispute. Of that, $1,436.31 is the 18-inbox charge (first month prorated $140.31 plus nine months at $144.00) and $107.77 is the domain year; $10.00 is the Legacy plan.

Forward exposure: $145.00 due 2026-10-02 and $108.00 due 2026-12-02, then $145.00 monthly, with no in-product cancellation path.

Why there is no cancel path (current code): the Billing page card renders from org mail_domain rows only and shows "No managed domains" when there are none, offering no Cancel control; cancellation runs through cancelManagedDomains, which returns "Domain is not managed by this workspace" when no mail_domain row exists. Cancelling the named plan product cancels only that product, which is the $1 reduction the customer saw. Repository HEAD read: f0228bab1e57b287a17a66e2e042abc3de8191dd.

Discretion: needs-human. All three systems of record agree the add-ons are live and paid, so this is not a sync fault; the divergence is between what was paid for and what exists in the workspace. No prior approval or promise exists in the conversation or the request, so the amount decision is a person's.

Proposed human action (proposal, not a promise):

1. Cancel the live Inbox add-on ($8 x 18) and the Domain add-on on billing account 7de4ed09.../Stripe subscription <stripe-id> before the 2026-10-02 renewal, so the October and December charges cannot land.
2. Decide the refund: $1,436.31 for inbox capacity never created plus an amount for the domain year the customer never had visible, out of $1,554.08 collected. No refund or credit has been issued.
3. Tell the customer, because he has had no answer since Fin AI escalated him on 2026-09-29.

Unverified on this ticket: the customer's purchase intent at signup; whether the December 2025 order flow code matches today's HEAD, so no failing function is attributed; the provider-side cancellation record for these six domains (the cancellation log table starts 2026-08-01 and holds no row for them).

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer's cancellation request left a $129 past-due subscription with a retry scheduled, on the billing account they never cancelled
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom source: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: Contact (Name 10, <email>) opened on 2026-09-30 asking to cancel his domains and Cold Email Agent (AI SDR) client and to stop being billed. Fin AI answered with self-serve cancellation steps and closed the conversation; the contact reopened it and asked for a human. His final message: "I've gone through the process of cancelling one of the subaccouts (Company One) and the domains/inboxes and further billing. However, I was attempted to be billed yesterday and it did not go through. I want the charges to be cancelled and not attempted to bill me again." No amount, invoice id, or date was named. No prior approval, promise, coupon, or discretionary credit appears anywhere in the thread.

Account: this contact is the owner of two workspaces. Company One, Inc. (created 2026-05-20) carries the domains, inboxes and paid plan. Name 10's Workspace (created 2025-07-14) is the personal $1 Legacy workspace he enrolled first.

Ask (classify_ask): money, bucket 'overcharged'. Two distinct things are mixed in one message: stopping a failed charge and its retry, and a prior billing discrepancy he has never itemized.

## Evidence

Systems of record, read in order.

PlanetScale (acquisity / main):

* Company One billing account 10e96d6f-...: subscriptionStatus null, subscriptionPlan null, domains balance 0, inboxes balance 0, no credit transactions. Its 10 mail_domain rows are all suspended as of 2026-09-30T00:26:57Z.
* The suspended domains sit under domain_purchase_order d9aaa5e6-... (created 2026-05-27, 10 domains ordered, 29/30 inboxes provisioned, completed 2026-05-28). A second order d0d8aa9b-... (2026-07-25, 20 domains) was cancelled by the user and never paid, so it never billed.
* Name 10's Workspace, billing account 32f7330c-..., is unchanged and still active.

Autumn:

* Company One (billing account 10e96d6f-...): one subscription, plan legacy_pro at $129/month, status active, past_due true, canceled_at 1790727969812 (2026-09-30, about 22:26 UTC, roughly 18 minutes before the contact's last Intercom message), expires_at 1793135024000, current_period_end 2026-10-27. The cancel was requested inside the product. No cancellations exist for the 10 domain line items or the 10 inbox line items, which is why the domains show suspended rather than cancelled.
* Name 10's Workspace (billing account 32f7330c-...): plan legacy at $1/month, active, its own Stripe customer <stripe-id>. It kept billing $1/month in Aug and Sep 2026.

Stripe:

* Company One, <stripe-id>, is delinquent and carries two subscriptions and two separate billing streams:
  * <stripe-id>, Legacy Pro $129/month. cancel_at 1793135024, so its next charge has already been stopped. Invoice <stripe-id> (OPDYCP6F-0010), 12900 USD, status open, amount_paid 0, attempt_count 1, next_payment_attempt 1790769908. That scheduled retry is the billing attempt the contact is asking us to stop. The period 2026-08-28 to 2026-09-27 was already collected earlier on charge <stripe-id> on 2026-09-08 after eight declines.
  * A second Legacy Pro subscription stream under a separate Stripe subscription, invoice OPDYCP6F-0009 (18000 USD, open, attempt_count 9) plus a domain/inbox stream that last billed 18000 USD on invoice OPDYCP6F-0007 (paid 2026-08-24).
  * Every open charge on this customer is a failed attempt: status failed, card_declined, insufficient_funds (issuer decline code 51), amount_captured 0. No money was collected on any of them.
  * Total actually taken from this account in Aug and Sep 2026: 18000 + 12900 = 30900 USD. No refunds and no credit notes exist on the account.
* Name 10's Workspace, <stripe-id>, is current and not delinquent.

Name 11:

* No Inngest or Sentry lane was needed to explain the charge itself; the divergence is fully explained by the reads above.

## First divergent hop

Not a system-to-system break: Stripe, Autumn and the workspace disagree about nothing. The gap is between the contact's belief about what he cancelled and what the product cancelled. He cancelled the plan on the Company One workspace, which set the subscription to cancel at period end, and the domains/inboxes were suspended, but the already-issued open invoice for the running period still has a retry scheduled, and the domain/inbox line items were never cancelled as subscriptions.

## Verification

The in-app billing page he was looking at shows the open $129 charge while the plan already reads as cancelled, which is exactly the "billing error/discrepancy" he reported. That reading is consistent with the Stripe state and is a product presentation issue, not a data error.

## What is not established

What the earlier discrepancy he referred to on 2026-09-30 consisted of. He never named an amount, invoice, or date, and nothing in the account shows a charge that overstates what he was entitled to for the periods billed. The outstanding retry and the residual domain/inbox subscription state are the only unresolved money items.

## Unblock and open human decision

Two separate things need a human, and neither is money we can move automatically:

1. Stop the next charge. Cancel the two open invoices' retry (next_payment_attempt 1790769908 on invoice <stripe-id>) and cancel the domain/inbox line items that are still live on the Company Five billing account so nothing is attempted again.
2. Decide the old discrepancy. Once he names what he believes is wrong, decide whether any refund is owed. Nothing collected after the cancellation date is refundable, because nothing was collected after it.

relatedSnapshot.title: Flag inactive CMR domains that are still billed as overcharged
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Since Acquisity/Acquisity#6595, the CMR Domain Subscription Audit records domains that are INACTIVE or EXPIRED at ColdMailReseller as `cmr_inactive`. It doesn't check whether the customer is still being billed for them, so a customer paying for a domain that no longer exists at CMR looks identical to one who stopped paying.

There is also a quieter bug: a dedicated billing subscription for an inactive domain went into the group's shared pool and could count as coverage for an active domain, hiding an unpaid active domain.

## Root cause

Classification only matched billing subscriptions against active domains. Anything attached to an inactive domain was treated as unmatched pool coverage, and inactive domains were never compared against billing.

## Solution

* Match subscriptions against every domain in a billing group. A subscription dedicated to an inactive domain stays with that domain and no longer covers active ones.
* New payment state `overcharged` for an inactive domain that is still billed. It applies when either:
  * its dedicated domain/inbox subscription is active and not scheduled to end, or
  * pooled (unmatched) billing covers more domains/inboxes than the group's active domains need. Surplus is assigned to inactive domains alphabetically: one domain each, inboxes up to each domain's inbox count. If the surplus comes from the billing feature ledger, the note says it may include comped grants.
* Billing already scheduled to end is not flagged. The domain stays `cmr_inactive` with "billing ends YYYY-MM-DD" in the note.
* Groups where every domain is inactive now get a billing lookup (Acquisity/Acquisity#6595 skipped this).
* `overcharged` has severity 3, is included in "Action needed", the run summary's actionable list, and a new "Overcharged" tab with an amber badge. It is not a CMR-cancellable state (the domain is already dead at CMR; the fix is on the billing side) but it can be dismissed.
* Migration widens `cmr_domain_audit_finding_payment_state_check` with `overcharged` using `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE`, following Acquisity/Acquisity#6595.

## Impact

* **User:** none directly. Admins can now find customers paying for dead domains and refund/cancel that billing.
* **Business:** catches overbilling before it becomes a support ticket or chargeback, and stops inactive domains hiding underpayment on active ones.

## Testing

7 new unit tests covering: a dedicated subscription still billing an inactive domain; an inactive domain's subscription no longer covering an active one; surplus from pooled domain billing; surplus from pooled inbox billing split across inactive domains; billing scheduled to end; surplus from the billing feature ledger; and groups where every domain is inactive. Audit, admin, renewal, cancel suites and the snapshot DB test (which applies the migration) also pass.

## Notes

* Expect some active domains to move from `paid` to `unpaid`/`underpaid` on the first run.
* When overcharge comes from pooled billing, which inactive domain carries it is arbitrary; the group total is correct.
* Not covered: billing for domains that have disappeared from CMR entirely (no finding row to attach it to).
* Rollback: revert the PR. The widened constraint is harmless if left in place.

Follows Acquisity/Acquisity#6595.

relatedSnapshot.title: Billing card shows CMR-ended domains as Active while they are still billed
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The CMR domain audit marks a domain `overcharged` when CMR has ended it but Autumn/Whop billing still renews (e.g. a domain cancelled in CMR on Sep 25 with inbox billing still renewing Oct 25).

The **customer** billing card had no case for `overcharged`, so those domains showed:

* no billing badge
* inboxes labelled **Active**
* a **"Payment due"** countdown

So a customer paying for a domain that no longer exists saw the opposite of the truth, with no signal that anything was wrong. The admin side has flagged this since ENG-14258; the customer side never did.

## Solution

* `DomainBillingBadge`: `overcharged` renders **"Ended <date> · Still billed"** (warning) with a tooltip telling the customer to cancel to stop billing.
* New `isOverchargedDomainBilling` and `isEndedDomainBilling` helpers.
* `EmailAccountsDomainsCard`: for ended domains (inactive or overcharged), inboxes show **"Ended"** and the payment-due column is hidden.
* The **Cancel button stays** for overcharged domains — `cancelManagedDomainInProvider` already treats CMR "already cancelled / not found" as success, so cancelling proceeds to cancel the billing. This is the customer's self-serve fix.

## Regression guard

Adds a test that **every** audit payment state renders a badge except the internal `unlinked` and `error`, so a newly added state cannot silently render nothing again — which is exactly how this bug arose when `overcharged` was introduced.

## Testing

* `bunx vitest run tests/components/billing/domain-billing-badge.test.tsx` — 11 passed.
* Biome, tsc on changed files, `check-v2 --changed` clean.

## Coordination note

Acquisity/Acquisity#6642 (ENG-14340) also edits `email-accounts-domains-card.tsx` and is still open. The two are logically consistent — ENG-14340 hides Cancel for `cmr_inactive` (nothing left to cancel), this one deliberately keeps it for `overcharged` (billing is still running, so cancelling is the fix) — but they will likely conflict in that file. Worth landing them in a deliberate order.

## Notes

3 files, +55/-4. Part of the CMR domain audit series.

relatedSnapshot.title: Docs Gap: Help Center does not explain unpaid/"Open" invoices appearing as a second Pro charge
relatedSnapshot.description:
DOCS GAP: The Billing docs (`apps/web/content/docs/workspace-settings/billing.mdx`) have an "I was charged twice" troubleshooting entry, but it only covers prorated plan changes and credit-pack overlap. Nothing explains billing-history invoice statuses — specifically that an invoice marked **Open** is an *unpaid/failed* charge, not money collected, and that a failed Pro renewal can sit as an Open invoice while a later successful re-subscription creates a second Pro line item on a different date. Customers (and Fin) read this as two active Pro subscriptions. The "My payment failed" entry also says "the system will try again automatically" but does not say what happens after retries are exhausted (subscription canceled, invoice left Open, resubscribe required).

CUSTOMER CONTEXT: Name 14 (<email>, workspace `<workspace-slug>`) saw a Pro charge dated Jul 8 ($185, status Open) and another Pro charge dated Jul 25 ($184.25) and believed he was paying for two Pro subscriptions. Evidence: Stripe customer `<stripe-id>` — invoice `<stripe-id>` (Jul 8, $185) is still **open** with 9 failed payment attempts ("The connection to the user's Link account has been closed"); the original Pro subscription `<stripe-id>...` was canceled 2026-07-22 after dunning; a new Pro was purchased 2026-07-25 (`<stripe-id>...`, $184.25, paid). Autumn shows exactly one active `pro` product plus inbox/domain add-ons. Only one Pro payment was ever collected per period — no duplicate subscription.

SUGGESTED CONTENT: Add a Help Center section "Understanding your billing history statuses" (Paid / Open / Void / Uncollectible) with an explicit note that Open = never charged, and extend the "My payment failed" accordion with what happens when retries run out (plan canceled, unpaid invoice stays visible, how to resubscribe). Also add a bullet to "I was charged twice": "If one of the charges is marked Open, it was never collected."

RELATED DOC(S):

* <url:app.acquisity.ai> (Troubleshooting → "I was charged twice", "My payment failed")
* Fin answered this conversation with an incorrect "prorated adjustment" explanation; the source content should be corrected so Fin stops asserting proration for failed-payment cases.
